## Task 1. Short-form video (about 45 minutes)

Make a 30 to 60 second video introducing Ajaia to someone who has never heard of us. Build it from what is on ajaia.ai: the copy, the service lines, the products, screen recordings of the site, plus any stock, motion, AI-generated, or self-recorded footage you want to add.

Pick the platform first. Instagram Reels, TikTok, LinkedIn, or YouTube Shorts. Tell us which one, and cut for that platform's format and behavior.

**Deliver:** the video link, plus five bullets covering the platform you chose and why, the hook and why it earns the next three seconds, one thing you deliberately cut, one thing you would test in a second version, and the one metric you would watch.

## Task 2. Instagram set (about 30 minutes)

Design a set for the Ajaia Instagram:

- One carousel, three to five slides, 1080 x 1080
- One story frame, 1080 x 1920
- One caption for the carousel, under 150 words

Subject is yours to pick, as long as it is Ajaia or AI at work. Explaining a service line, an idea about AI adoption, a myth worth killing, a stat worth reframing. Build a look that could plausibly be ours and hold it across all the assets. Any tool.

**Deliver:** the files or a link to them, plus two sentences on the visual system you chose and what you would change if this were slide one of thirty.

## Task 3. Write something about AI (about 25 minutes)

Write a piece for LinkedIn on any angle about AI you actually have a view on. Adoption, jobs, hype, tooling, what people get wrong, what you have seen change in your own work.

250 words minimum. There is no maximum. If the argument needs a thousand words, write a thousand words. Length is not the grade, but nothing gets a pass for being long, and every extra paragraph has to earn its place.

Have a point of view. Take a position someone could disagree with. Do not write a summary of what AI is. Do not write "AI is transforming everything." If we can predict your third sentence from your first, it is not working.

Nothing you cannot support. No invented statistics.

## Task 4. Walk us through it (about 15 minutes)

Record 3 to 5 minutes of yourself walking us through what you made. Unedited. Phone camera is fine. Share your screen and show the work if you want.

Cover, in order:

- What you made and the thinking behind each piece
- The single decision you are least sure about
- What you would do with four more hours
- How you used AI: what you asked for, what you kept, what you rejected and why
- Your hourly rate expectation and how many hours a week you can work

This is the piece we watch first. It is where taste is easiest to hear.

## AI Workflow Note (150 words max, write it as you go)

List every AI tool you used and for what. Then name the single most useful thing AI produced for you today, and the single worst, and what you did about the worst.

## Optional. Anything you have already made

If you have work you are proud of, drop the links at the end. An account, videos, designs, writing, a project that went nowhere but taught you something. Personal projects count fully. This is optional and adds to your score. Leaving it blank does not subtract from it.

## Submission checklist

- Task 1 video link plus five bullets
- Task 2 carousel, story frame, and caption
- Task 3 written piece, 250 words or more
- Task 4 walkthrough video, 3 to 5 minutes
- AI Workflow Note
- Optional prior work links
- Every link opens for anyone with the link. Check this in a private browser window.
